declared.title: A meta-analysis of the efficacy of acceptance and commitment therapy for clinically relevant mental and physical health problems
declared.foundIn: docs/design/review-science.md (dossier du pilote, 2026-11-22) ; titre de mémoire de la session

findings.text: A therapy built on acceptance (ACT) works about as well as CBT, not better

support.sentence: The comparison between ACT and established treatments (cognitive behavioral therapy) did not reveal any significant differences between these treatments (p = 0.140).

findings.text: ACT works better than no treatment, placebo or usual care

support.sentence: ACT outperformed control conditions (Hedges' g = 0.57) at posttreatment and follow-up assessments in completer and intent-to-treat analyses for primary outcomes.

limits: ACT is a whole program, not acceptance alone
allegiance: includes data provided by the ACBS community, the association that develops and promotes ACT
